I will keep my land split between the wheat-maize rotation and cotton, because I have only 10.1 mu, my household labor is limited, and some family members work off-farm. I want a plan that is steady, familiar, and manageable with well irrigation. I will put 6.1 mu into the wheat-maize rotation and 4.0 mu into cotton. For wheat, I will use improved seed, keep fertilizer at a moderate level, irrigate three times, and aim for a stable yield instead of pushing too hard. After wheat harvest, I will plant summer maize on the same 6.1 mu, use hybrid seed, reduce tillage to save labor, and rely on one to two irrigations depending on rainfall. For cotton, I will keep the area smaller because it takes more field management and pest control, but I will still grow it because it spreads risk and fits my experience. I will manage cotton with moderate fertilizer, a few irrigations, and more pesticide sprays than grain crops because insects are usually a bigger problem there.
